profileIsolation: Verified from the running process --user-data-dir argument. The app DB and artifacts in this report are under the temporary profile.

checks.detail: Onboarding accepted the local LM Studio endpoint. Health showed the configured model available. Chat and Work selection worked. Agent was disabled while no workspace was bound.
Displayed the requested short response. SQLite records one model call and state Completed.

Created a second chat while the first Chat response was active. The first response stayed with its owner. Work then ran in a separate chat while another Chat request displayed Waiting for local inference. The queued Chat request was stopped and recorded Cancelled; Work remained in its own chat.

Work saved ui-check.md with the exact requested 28 bytes. Independent SHA-256 matched SQLite. UI showed File saved and Partial because required acceptance evidence was unverified. The run snapshot persisted Partial.

Quit the directly launched isolated app and reopened it with the same temporary profile. All three chats returned. The Work artifact, run ID and Partial status returned. The Resume from saved evidence action was visible and not invoked.
Agent was disabled without a workspace. Selecting a new empty temporary directory showed that workspace root and enabled Agent.

Twice, including in a fresh chat, the model proposed Write smoke.txt plus an unrelated generate_deliverable action for smoke.docx, despite explicit instructions not to create an artifact. The app showed both operations in its approval gate. Both plans were rejected. SQLite records both rejections and Cancelled run states. smoke.txt remains BEFORE and no other workspace file exists.
Queued cancellation and cancellation at the plan-approval gate were checked. The active transport Stop button was not separately exercised in this UI pass.

defaultProfileIncident.detail: During the first UI restart, macOS brought up a second app process without the temporary profile argument. The process started in the default app data directory and touched its workbench.db. I did not submit a prompt to it or inspect conversation data, then quit it. No before-run snapshot was taken, so its prior database state cannot be established. All subsequent test steps used the direct executable with the verified temporary-profile argument.

limits: No Python fallback approval dialog was exercised.
The test workspace and profile hold disposable test data in /tmp. The profile is under 1 MB; no source workspace files were changed.
